Definition: apparently a primary verb; to be beforehand, i.e. anticipate or precede; by extension, to have arrived at:--(already) attain, come, prevent.
BiblicalUsage: Phthano means to come before, to anticipate, to arrive first, and it appears where the kingdom arrives. Jesus says that if He casts out devils by the Spirit of God, then the kingdom of God is come unto you, and Paul says wrath has come upon the unbelieving Jews to the uttermost.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that the kingdom does not creep: it comes, it arrives, and when it comes it is already here, whether men welcome it or not.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
